newsitem.title: USA: New Glaxo drug seen highlight at AIDS meet.
newsitem.headline: New Glaxo drug seen highlight at AIDS meet.

text.p: A new drug for AIDS patients, "1592", manufactured by Glaxo Wellcome Plc, would be among others receiving attention at this week's AIDS convention in Washington, said Barron's columnist Alan Abelson.
In his "Up & Down Wall Street" column, Abelson wrote that 1592 has been described as a "chemical cousin" to its well known AZT drug, but showing fewer of the negative aspects of AZT.

Abelson said AIDS activists were pressuring the company to accelerate its availability. He said expectations now are for the drug to be available in about seven months, and that 1592 would "rapidly replace both AZT and 3TC and importantly improve the effectiveness of AIDS therapy."

Also expected to be closely watched are new protease inhibitors which, when combined with nucleoside analog drugs such as AZT and 3TC, have been especially effective in slowing the growth of the HIV virus.
Abelson mentioned new protease inhibitors expected from Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc and Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc as among those to watch.
